RSV vehicle register (Ministry of Transport open data): new N1 vans (incl. N1G), monthly from 2016-01, counted by their first Czech registration. Until 2026-09 this was a quarterly ACEA series with BEV and PHEV merged (kept as data/Czechia_legacy.csv). The register counts about 2-3 % fewer vans than SDA/ACEA, and up to a quarter fewer electric vans since 2025: SDA also counts vans first registered abroad shortly before import, which the register files as used. Full and mild hybrids are inside PETROL/DIESEL (the register cannot tell them apart).

RSV vehicle register (Ministry of Transport open data): new N2 + N3 lorries and tractor units (incl. off-road G), monthly from 2016-01. About 1 % below SDA/ACEA; BEV counts agree. Until 2026-09 a quarterly ACEA series (kept as data/Czechia_legacy.csv). Hybrids without a plug are inside PETROL/DIESEL.

RSV vehicle register (Ministry of Transport open data): new M2 + M3 buses and coaches (incl. off-road G), monthly from 2016-01; matches SDA/ACEA to within a few vehicles a quarter. Low volume (roughly 50-200 a month), so the share swings with fleet orders. Until 2026-09 a quarterly ACEA series (kept as data/Czechia_legacy.csv). Hybrids without a plug are inside PETROL/DIESEL.

New passenger cars (M1 incl. off-road M1G). History: SDA (the importers' association) via ACEA. From 2026-09 each month is first written from the RSV vehicle register (Ministry of Transport open data) on the 1st-3rd: BEV, PHEV, other fuels and TOTAL are register counts (TOTAL within 0.0-0.9 % of SDA/ACEA since 2025, BEV within a few cars), while HEV/PETROL/DIESEL are an estimate in the previous ACEA month's proportions, because the register does not record mild and most full hybrids. When ACEA publishes the month (third to fourth week) its official figures replace the row; until then the generated posts give no HEV share for that month. A month ACEA never publishes (July) keeps the register row, flagged in its notes. 2016-2021 have no HEV split (hybrids inside PETROL/DIESEL).

RSV vehicle register (Ministry of Transport open data): used passenger cars (M1/M1G) at their first Czech registration — imports first registered abroad, dated by the month they entered the Czech register; monthly from 2016-01. A different population from new registrations (around 12,000-15,000 a month, about 10 years old on average). Plug-ins are recognised by the register's hybrid class or a combined CO2 of at most 60 g/km; full and mild hybrids are inside PETROL/DIESEL.

ASTRA register data (IVZ open data), CH + Liechtenstein: new M2/M3 buses and coaches over 3.5 t (ACEA's definition), monthly from 2016-01. Very low volume (roughly 30-90 a month), so the share swings with fleet orders. Until 2026-09 a quarterly ACEA series (kept as data/Switzerland_legacy.csv).

New passenger cars in Switzerland and Liechtenstein (one register). From 2026-09 ASTRA register data (IVZ open data), calibrated to ACEA: 2025-01..2026-08 total -0.02 %, BEV +0.1 %. History: ASTRA from 2022 (rebuilt), BFS before (which also counts used imports, so slightly higher), ACEA 2026-04..08 (2026-07 derived from year-to-date sums). HEV includes mild hybrids.
ASTRA register data (IVZ open data), CH + Liechtenstein: new mopeds and motorcycles (EU L1 + L3), monthly from 2016-01. Trikes, sidecars and quads excluded. Strongly seasonal (spring peak).

ASTRA register data (IVZ open data, GEBR): used passenger cars at their first Swiss registration — used imports first registered abroad, dated by the month they entered the Swiss register. From 2017-01. A different population from new registrations; plug-ins before 2022 are recognised by CO2 only.

DNRPA registry: new passenger-car body types (~EU M1) of every brand. Records carry no fuel field - powertrain classified from the model name and checked against ACARA's electrified totals; MHEV is a lower bound; no petrol/diesel split.
DNRPA registry: Whole where the first owner is a natural person (persona física). Private + Industry = Whole. Powertrain classified from the model name.
DNRPA registry: Whole where the first owner is a legal person (companies / state / fleets). Private + Industry = Whole. Powertrain classified from the model name.

MIA vehicle register (data.gov.ua), record level: first registrations of new passenger cars (KIND 'passenger', EU M1) by the register's own new-vehicle operation codes, from 2018-09. The register reports a single combined hybrid figure (no PHEV/HEV/MHEV split): shown as 'Hybrid' in the fuel-split chart; counted within ICE in the BEV/ICE trajectory, which omits a PHEV curve. The Dec-2025 BEV spike and 2026 drop coincide with the end of the VAT exemption for EV imports on 2026-01-01 (pull-forward).
MIA vehicle register: Whole where the owner is a natural person (PERSON = P). Private + Industry = Whole. Combined hybrid bucket, no PHEV split.
MIA vehicle register: Whole where the owner is a legal person (companies, state, fleets; PERSON = J). Private + Industry = Whole. Combined hybrid bucket, no PHEV split.

MIA vehicle register: used passenger cars at their first Ukrainian registration (used imports, by the register's own used-vehicle operation codes). A different population from new registrations; customs-policy changes (2020-2022 legalisation wave, 2026 VAT on EV imports) move it in steps. Combined hybrid bucket.
MIA vehicle register: new goods vehicles with a gross vehicle weight up to 3,500 kg (EU N1), by the register's new-vehicle operation codes.

Transport Department record-level first registrations (DATA.GOV.HK): private cars never registered abroad (TD status A/B/C1, EU M1), from 2019-11; matches TD's own table 4.1(e). TD's fuel field has no hybrid value: plug-in hybrids are classified from the model name (few: ~1% of new cars), full and mild hybrids are counted in PETROL. Taxis excluded. The EV first-registration-tax concession was cut for applications from 1 Apr 2024 and ended from 1 Apr 2026: registrations spike just before each date and the BEV share steps down after it (a policy effect, not noise).

Transport Department records: private cars registered abroad before import (TD status C2) — used imports, dominated by Japanese-market Toyota and Honda MPVs (Alphard, Vellfire, Voxy; median model year 2019 in the year to Jul 2026). A different population from new registrations. Hybrids counted in PETROL; plug-ins classified from the model name.

Transport Department records: new light goods vehicles with a permitted gross weight up to 3.5 t (EU N1; TD status A/B/C1/E). Hong Kong's LGV class runs to 5.5 t — the heavier ones are excluded. Low volume (roughly 30-500 a month, falling since 2023).

MOTIR monthly press release (data: KAMA + KAIDA): domestic sales of all vehicle types — passenger cars and commercial vehicles, not EU M1 — domestic makers plus imports. Sales, not registrations. Imported hybrids include mild hybrids. Tesla is not counted before 2024 (importers' association coverage), so BEV is understated up to 2023. No petrol/diesel split; ICE = total minus eco-friendly cars; hydrogen in Others. Hand-entered 2017-2024, automated and cross-checked from 2025.

SUNARP first registrations of new vehicles as compiled by the Asociación Automotriz del Perú (public BI-AAP report), from 2019-01: cars, station wagons, SUVs and MPVs (EU M1); minibuses excluded. Pickups are NOT in Whole — they are counted in Peru (Vans), unlike e.g. Thailand where pickups sit inside the headline series. Matches AAP's printed monthly totals exactly. AAP re-classifies the BEV/PHEV/HEV split of earlier months after the fact (totals unchanged), so older rows can shift by a few units at each update. HEV includes mild hybrids (the registry only separated them in 2025). No registrations in April 2020 (COVID-19 lockdown, registry closed) — that month has no row. AAP reports these as new-vehicle sales; used imports are only allowed up to two model years old, so a small near-new remainder may be included.

SUNARP first registrations (via AAP BI-AAP): pickups, chassis-cabs, dropside and box vans, and panel vans (EU N1), from 2019-01. Diesel-dominated; plug-ins are a handful a month (JAC T8 EV, BYD Shark).

Customs imports, not registrations: new cars (NCM 87.03, declared NUEVO) imported for consumption, from DNIT's record-level open data, from 2017-01. Paraguay has no car industry, so imports are the market (the distributors' chamber CADAM measures it the same way); single months can run ahead of sales when importers stock up. Powertrain = the tariff subheading (HS 2017): HEV includes mild hybrids. Pickups (NCM 87.04) are not included. Electrified imports match CADAM's yearly figures 2021-2025 within 2-6 %.

New cars and SUVs sold, from the tax authority SRI's record-level register of new-vehicle invoices (open data), from 2018-01: SRI classes AUTOMOVIL + JEEP (EU M1, = AEADE's 'automóvil' + 'SUV'); pickups and vans are in Ecuador (Vans). Each vehicle counted once, in the month SRI first processed it; matches AEADE's published market within about 1 % a month. The register has a single hybrid code: plug-ins (PHEV, EREV) are picked out by this project's published rule table on the model (2025 within 0.3 % of ZEMO's count, 5 % below AEADE's yearbook); the remaining full and mild hybrids are HEV, counted within ICE. Nissan e-POWER (no plug) counts as HEV, not BEV.

SRI new-vehicle register: class CAMIONETA — pickups (most of it), panel vans and van-based minibuses (≈ EU N1; some passenger minivans included), from 2018-01. Diesel-dominated; plug-ins about 40 a month in 2026 (BYD Shark, Changan Hunter REEV), BEVs about 10 (Riddara RD6, BYD T3). Plug-ins from the same rule table as Ecuador (Whole).

New passenger cars (THB vehicle kind 'small passenger car', up to 9 seats, EU M1; taxis and rental cars included) from the Highway Bureau register, as published in the MOTC statistics database, from 2021-01. BEV, PHEV, EREV and HEV are THB's own fuel categories; HEV includes Nissan e-POWER, and 48 V mild hybrids sit in petrol or hybrid as their type approval says. Before 2021 THB's plug-in code still held conventional hybrids, so the series starts in 2021. Hybrids are 39 % of new cars and count within ICE. Monthly BEV counts swing with Tesla's quarter-end delivery waves (about 60 % of BEVs) — read the trend.

THB register (MOTC statistics): new goods vehicles up to 3.5 t ('small goods vehicle' ≈ EU N1), from 2021-01 — since 2020-09-04 also 3.5–5 t vehicles up to 6 m long. Pickups, panel vans and small cab-over trucks; roughly half petrol, half diesel; BEV under 1 %.

THB register (MOTC statistics): new goods vehicles over 3.5 t ('large goods vehicle' ≈ EU N2+N3, tractor units included), from 2021-01 — since 2020-09-04 without the 3.5–5 t vehicles up to 6 m long (now in Vans). Almost entirely diesel.

THB register (MOTC statistics): new buses and coaches ('large passenger vehicle': 10+ seats or over 3.5 t, EU M2+M3), city buses and tour coaches together, from 2021-01. Small and lumpy (100–200 a month, fleet batches); the BEV share reflects the government's city-bus electrification programme.

New car registrations compiled by SMMT from DVLA data (passenger cars, all brands). Mild hybrids are counted inside petrol and diesel, as SMMT publishes them; full hybrids (HEV) count within ICE. March and September are plate-change months with about a quarter of the year's registrations each — compare single months with the same month a year earlier.
